description: Curated terminology and sources for HIV/AIDS, including testing, prevention, treatment, research, daily life, caregiving and advocacy. This pack is not medical advice.

synopsis.overview: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) attacks the immune system. Without treatment it can progress to advanced HIV or AIDS, a stage in which serious opportunistic infections and some cancers can occur.
synopsis.manifestations: Some people develop a short flu-like illness soon after infection, while others have no symptoms for years. Untreated HIV gradually weakens immune defences; the only way to know HIV status is through testing.
synopsis.management: There is no cure, but antiretroviral therapy can suppress the virus to an undetectable level and protect the immune system. Ongoing care includes viral-load monitoring, prevention and treatment of other infections, and support for physical and mental health.
synopsis.outlook: With effective, sustained treatment, most people with HIV can live a long and healthy life and do not develop AIDS. A person who maintains an undetectable viral load does not transmit HIV through sex; outcomes are poorer when diagnosis or effective treatment is delayed.
